Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-25
Start: 15:00 EST
Duration: 57 minutes
Recording id: ff-20251125-7649
Attendees: Tara Nguyen (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendez (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (HorizonCare Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Infra Engineer), Jordan Blake (CTO)
Artifacts mentioned: dedicated-pricing.pdf, sla-attachments.pdf, horizon-prompt-set.csv (link shared in chat), perf-baseline.xlsx

Summary:
High-level discovery focused on dedicated (reserved) GPU capacity for HorizonCare's private inference needs. Discussed isolation requirements for PHI workloads, burst capacity model, autoscaling/cooldown expectations, acceptable tail latency (95th/99th), and steps for a short pilot and benchmarks. Agreed actions: Redwood to share pricing and SLA materials, SE to run benchmarks on Horizon prompt set, schedule architecture deep-dive for private deployment.

Topics covered:
- Dedicated capacity sizing and reservation options
- Tenant isolation / VPC/private deployment concerns (KMS, audit logs)
- Burst policies and fallback routing to hosted instances
- Tail latency vs batching tradeoffs and KV cache warmup
- Pilot scope and timeline

Action items (recap):
- Tara: pricing + SLA + security summary
- Carlos: perf benchmarks and tail-latency report
- Priya: share prompt set and expected peak qps patterns

Transcript body:
[00:00] Tara Nguyen: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro, i'm tara from redwood, i'm the AE on this account. carlos will jump in on the technicals. how's everyone doing?
[00:10] Jordan Blake: good thanks, short on time but excited to dig in.
[00:15] Priya Shah: morning, thanks. i'll try to keep this focused — we want to understand dedicated options and whether private is worth the lift.
[00:22] Carlos Mendez: cool, i'll kick off with a quick overview of what dedicated looks like — reserved GPU pools, optional single-tenant isolation, and burst lanes to our hosted pool if you need extra qps. then we can map that to your constraints.
[00:35] Liam O'Connor: quick clarifying q — by isolation do you mean physical tenancy or logical? our security team is pretty strict since we handle PHI.
[00:44] Carlos Mendez: good question. we offer both levels. physical-tenancy is available for dedicated nodes so you don't share the GPU host with other customers; logical isolation is via strict networking and runtime tenanting. for private VPC deployments we can go on-prem or VPC with a private control plane. encryption is KMS-backed; HSM integrations available.
[01:05] Priya Shah: HSM is non-negotiable for us, and we need audit logs to cover model inputs — is that in place?
[01:12] Tara Nguyen: yes, our enterprise package includes audit logs that record request ids, model version, timestamps. we'll include the SOC2 section in the packet.
[01:20] Jordan Blake: how does burst work — say we reserve 8 A100s for steady load, but then we hit a marketing spike — can we burst to 16 or 24? and what's the SLA during bursts?
[01:33] Carlos Mendez: two options. one is a reserved pool with elastic burst capacity to our hosted fleet — that is best-effort for burst, with prioritized routing. second is a committed burst buffer: you buy a small burst reservation that sits idle until used, which keeps latency SLOs tighter. during best-effort bursts, routing may go to compatible model variants; we fall back to lower-precision quantized variants if needed to sustain qps while keeping latency reasonable.
[01:55] Priya Shah: falling back to quantized variants — do you have quality regression monitoring? our outputs need to pass medical QA.
[02:03] Carlos Mendez: yes, Redwood Optimize can attach evals to prompt sets to detect regressions. we can tie alerts to thresholds and roll back pinning. we'll include a sample eval run in the pilot.
[02:18] Liam O'Connor: what about cold-start tail latency? we saw in our tests that kv cache warmup was killing the 99th percentile.
[02:27] Carlos Mendez: right — KV cache warmup is huge. our runtime supports prefix caching and sticky routing so warm instances keep KV warm for hot keys. also, we do continuous micro-batching and can pre-warm with synthetic traffic during scheduled windows.
[02:45] Jordan Blake: what's the expected 95/99 latency for a 2k token avg workload on an A100 profile? just ballpark.
[02:53] Carlos Mendez: ballpark: 95th around 120–250ms depending on batching; 99th can be 300–600ms if cold. dedicated with pinned instances and burst buffer can push 99th closer to 250–350ms. we'll validate against your prompts.
[03:12] Priya Shah: we're aiming for sub-300ms 95th and sub-600ms 99th for our primary endpoint; any idea on token-cost tradeoffs? switching to 8-bit quant reduces cost but potentially hurts QA.
[03:23] Carlos Mendez: exactly — quantization is a cost lever. Redwood Optimize can recommend quant level per workload. during pilot we run quality vs cost matrix so you can pick the operating point.
[03:36] Tara Nguyen: curious about timeline — what's your desired go-live for dedicated?
[03:40] Jordan Blake: Q1 FY26 ideally; pilot in December/Jan to validate.
[03:45] Priya Shah: yes pilot first. we want to see no-PHI leakage, perf baselines, and an ops playbook for failover.
[03:52] Liam O'Connor: if we do private VPC, what network egress patterns exist? do you need open egress to your control plane?
[04:00] Carlos Mendez: for VPC private deployments, the control plane can be customer-hosted; otherwise our control plane will need limited egress for telemetry and billing. we can support air-gapped installs for highly regulated customers but that increases lead time.
[04:13] Priya Shah: ok noted. what's the typical lead time for an air-gapped/private on-prem deploy?
[04:18] Carlos Mendez: historically 8–12 weeks depending on procurement and infra readiness. VPC with private control plane is 4–6 weeks.
[04:26] Jordan Blake: pricing — can you share the reserved vs burst pricing breakdown? we have to model TCO.
[04:31] Tara Nguyen: yes, i'll send a dedicated pricing pdf. high level: reserved capacity priced monthly with discounts for annual commit; burst buffers priced as smaller monthly commitments. there's also an enterprise license for the private control plane.
[04:44] Priya Shah: do you expose per-token cost breakdowns? we want to map to business metrics for teams.
[04:50] Carlos Mendez: Console has token-level cost and latency breakdown, per-route dashboards, and cost-attribution. we'll show a demo in the architecture workshop.
[04:59] Liam O'Connor: do you support SAML SSO + RBAC for our teams?
[05:03] Tara Nguyen: yes, SAML, SCIM, and granular RBAC are supported. we'll add a security appendix for SSO and KMS.
[05:10] Jordan Blake: backup/failover question: if a dedicated pool fails, what's the fallback?
[05:16] Carlos Mendez: routing policies handle that — you can choose auto-failover to hosted equivalents, or to a lower-cost region. failover is configurable per-route and per-model; we keep version pinning so the app still gets the same model family, possibly quantized. we can set up canaries to test failover before wide rollout.
[05:34] Priya Shah: one more ask — we need a small POC: 3 reserved gpus, private VPC, run our prompt set at baseline qps, and measure latencies and quality. can you scope that?
[05:44] Carlos Mendez: yes. suggested pilot: 3x A100 reserved for 30 days with a burst buffer of 2 GPUs, private VPC, and a security review. SE will run perf tests and basic evals on the prompt set.
[05:58] Tara Nguyen: great. i'll summarize and share pricing and SLA. can we tentatively schedule the arch workshop for week of 12/8?
[06:05] Jordan Blake: yes that works for us.
[06:08] Priya Shah: i'll circulate prompts and peak qps by tomorrow.
[06:12] Tara Nguyen: perfect. thanks everyone.

End of recording.

Notes on transcription quality: some terms mis-transcribed in the live notes (e.g., "KV cash" vs KV cache, "cube-ernetes" for Kubernetes, "VPV" for VPC). speaker labels may shift in places where call had crosstalk. This export retains those minor errors to reflect typical Fireflies exports.
